newsitem.title: USA: USDA June 12 U.S. crop highlights--USDA.
newsitem.headline: USDA June 12 U.S. crop highlights--USDA.

text.p: U.S. farmers will reap 1.604 billion bushels of winter wheat, the Agriculture Department estimated Thursday, up 42 million bushels or three percent, thanks to good weather in the past month.
USDA pegged 1996/97 soybean ending stocks at 130 million bushels, up five million from May and lowest in 20 years.
This year's soybean crop was projected for a record 2.600 billion bushels and corn for 9.840 billion. Last month, USDA put soybeans at 2.600 billion bushels and corn at 9.840 billion.
All wheat was projected for 2.304 billion bushels and the new cotton crop at 18.50 million 480-lb bales.

With harvest in its early stages, winter wheat was forecast to average 39.3 bushels an acre, up 1.1 from May, with 40.85 million acres harvested. Kansas and Oklahoma recovered from a mid-April freeze to offset cool weather in other states.
On Monday the corn, winter wheat and cotton crops all were listed in better shape than the same point a year ago. Corn and soybean seedings were the largest since the early 1980s.
Winter wheat forecast was based on field surveys. Corn, wheat and soybean projections assume normal weather, yields.
